bugs.what: Lys and Tamsin were recruited on the promise of personal quests ('A Brother in the Company', 'What the Mine Took') that were never resolved, and unlike Brother Osk and Vell (whose arcs both got dedicated closing lines), neither Lys nor Tamsin got any epilogue mention at all despite being carried in the party the whole game.
bugs.where: final status epilogue after *** WIN: reach_at_rest ***

bugs.what: The WIN screen states 'You crossed into Marrowgate by the Keepers' old pilgrim stair, past St. Ashwyn's Perch, the quiet way,' but the status epilogue's own bullet list separately claims 'Last Light heard you went under the mountain on the Free Companies' word, not the crown's' -- two contradictory accounts of the same journey.
bugs.where: Hollow Throne WIN screen vs. status epilogue list

bugs.what: Reaching 'three hollows rested' and walking to the Hollow Throne lets you end the entire game on the next action, with zero warning that doing so permanently abandons every other open thread (four companion/faction quests were still active when I won).
bugs.where: The Hollow Throne, 'speak the Great Rite over the seat'

bugs.what: Collected three separate 'owed' bells/relics across three holds (the saint's bell from Fenmarch's drowned nave, a barnacled ship's bell and a corroded bell-tongue from the Weeping Caves and the Fallen Chantry) that never got any destination or use -- only one specific bell ('the Drowned Bell's old ship's-bell') ever had a 'give to Keeper Wren' option.
bugs.where: inventory, carried unused through the ending

bugs.what: Accepted 'Something in the Reed-Cuts' (Fenmarch eel-trader's torn traps) but never found any way to close it in Fenmarch; a near-identical 'thing tearing up nets' bone-eel fight exists in a different hold (Saltkerns' Weeping Caves) and could easily be mistaken for the same problem, but the quest tracker never marked the Fenmarch one done.
bugs.where: The Eel-Market, quest 'Something in the Reed-Cuts'

bugs.what: Berin on the Gullhaven quay says he owes the harbourmaster 6 gold and 'can't go home... not owing that,' clearly inviting help, but no dialogue option to pay it off ever appeared even after I had 30 gold.
bugs.where: The Quay, Gullhaven, talk to Berin

bugs.what: 'Climb for the scrap of cloth' is a DC9 grace check explicitly re-triable on failure with no stated cost, so it can just be spammed until the die cooperates, making the difficulty meaningless.
bugs.where: Crow Perch (Vale of Ash), 'climb for the scrap of cloth'

bugs.what: The Saltkerns 'Wreckers' Roost' (Captain Grael) and the Hollowbrook 'Toll Stones' camp (tollkeeper Grae) reuse near-identical room text and NPC description ('Watches you the way a shopkeeper watches a full pocket') almost verbatim, reading as the same encounter copy-pasted into two holds.
bugs.where: the Wreckers' Roost — fire / the Toll Stones — fire

bugs.what: Both the mound-warden and a mere-fisher in Barrowmere flag an active grave-robbing problem ('someone's been digging where they shouldn't... Warden hasn't caught them yet'), but no location or NPC tied to it was ever found despite fully exploring the downs (ring-ditch, causeway, mere-stone, toll stones, bone track).
bugs.where: Barrowmere, the Mere-Shore, ask a mere-fisher: trouble on the downs

confusions: The '(hostile, hpX/X)' tag reads identically for NPCs that turn out to have a peaceful pay-the-toll or talk-it-down resolution and for ones that only ever fight, so there's no way to tell in advance which encounters expect violence.

Hollowbrook's chandler openly sells 'things dug from mounds' as curios while the mound-warden condemns the digging one room over, but the game never lets you connect the two or challenge the chandler about it.
It's never clear which of the several bell/relic items picked up across three different holds are meant for the same Keepers' Hall tithe and which are just flavor loot with no destination at all.
Nothing signals that walking into the Hollow Throne room and choosing the Great Rite is a point of no return that ends the whole 600-turn playthrough on the spot.
suggestions: Give every 'owed' item a pickup line that either hints at its destination or flags it as a pure keepsake, so players stop hunting for a delivery point that doesn't exist.
Let 'Something in the Reed-Cuts' actually resolve in Fenmarch, or have its text point the player toward the Saltkerns bone-eel as the real culprit.
Add a soft warning before the Hollow Throne's ending choices ('this will end your story here') so players can finish open companion threads first if they want to.
Differentiate the two toll-camp bandit captains (Grael vs. Grae) with distinct flavor so they don't read as the same fight reused.
Add a real pay-off option for small dangling debts raised in dialogue (like Berin's 6 gold) once the player has the means.
Give every recruited companion a dedicated epilogue line even when their personal quest goes unfinished, the way Osk and Vell got but Lys and Tamsin didn't.
